newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BORDER TOWN SLUBICE WINS BATTLE WITH RIVER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BORDER TOWN SLUBICE WINS BATTLE WITH RIVER.

text.p: The Polish city of Slubice on the German border seemed to have won its almost two week battle against the swollen Oder River on Thursday as the local governor allowed the evacuated citizens to return on Friday.

"Because of the systematically falling water level in the Oder and the diminishing flood threat to Slubice, the governor has decided that as of August 8 the evacuation order for citizens is cancelled," the governor's spokeswoman said.

Grazyna Cudak told Reuters already more than half of the city's 18,000 inhabitants have returned even though the earlier evacuation order stands until Friday and the rest of the people would come back on Thursday evening or on Friday.
"The town will be fully safe when the water falls down to 370 cm. It is now (1100 GMT) at 513 cm and falling very nicely by 2-3 cm an hour," Cudak said.

She said that as the threat of flooding diminished the governor called off 200 of the 550 soldiers patrolling the city's sodden dikes, cut down the police force to 170 from 400 people, and reduced border guard and firebrigade staff.
"Our efforts are now focused on patrolling the dikes and reinforcing their base, but the immediate flooding threat is gone," Cudak said.

She said the pedestrian border crossing in Slubice, across Germany's Frankfurt an der Oder, would be opened on Monday, but the car crossing would take longer, because Polish and German authorities had to make sure bridges were safe for traffic.

In early July Poland has been hit by the worst floods in centuries which inundated a total of 6,600 sq km killing 54 forcing tens of thousands out of their homes and causing damage of billions of dollars.
Nearly 1,700 sq km were still under water on Thursday and over 30,000 people remained displaced, but the floodwaters were receding.

Its retreat, however, presented the authorities with a huge clean-up problem as the water left behind garbage strewn over destroyed streets and buildings as well as rotting carcasses of drowned animals, mud and swarms of insects.

Cudak said that even though Slubice seemed to have escaped the flood, all cellars in the city were filled with water because of the high level of ground water, which also caused the city's sewage system to overflow.

"Experts say it is too early to start pumping out the water from the cellars because it is still high in the river, so for now we have make do with using chamicals to kill of the insects breeding there," Cudak said.
